| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InputGroup`          | native div props         | The frame; `role="group"`, focus and invalid state via `:has()`. |
| `InputGroupAddon`     | `align`, native div      | `inline-start \| inline-end \| block-start \| block-end`, `data-align`. |
| `InputGroupButton`    | `size`, `variant`, `type`| `xs \| sm \| icon-xs \| icon-sm`; ghost by default.            |
| `InputGroupText`      | native span props        | Muted text or an icon; not a label.                            |
| `InputGroupInput`     | `input` props            | Control with the frame's chrome removed; `data-slot="input-group-control"`. |
| `InputGroupTextarea`  | `textarea` props         | Same, for multi-line.                                          |

The frame watches `[data-slot=input-group-control]` for `:focus-visible` and
`[aria-invalid=true]`, which is why the control can be borderless and the group still
shows the ring.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). The frame never animates. `transition-[color,box-shadow]` covers the
focus ring and the invalid border — state feedback that takes no space and does not
run on mount.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

## Validation and data ownership

P11: the group shows invalid state, it never decides it.

| `InputGroup` does                                        | You do                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draws the destructive border when a control is invalid    | Deciding what is invalid                                 |
| Moves focus to the input when the addon is clicked        | Wiring `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`             |
| Renders the buttons you give it                           | Submit, retry, error mapping                             |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `resolver` prop, and no validation library is
imported. See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Accessibility

- The addon text is not a name. Give the control an `aria-label`, or put a `FieldLabel`
  around the group through `field`.
- `role="group"` on the frame and on each addon groups the pieces for assistive tech;
  add `aria-label` to the frame only if the group needs a name of its own.
- The addon focuses the input on click — a convenience for pointer users. Keyboard
  users tab straight into the control, which is already the shortest path.
- Buttons inside the frame keep their own names. An icon-only clear button needs
  `aria-label="Clear"`.
- `aria-invalid` must be on the control, not on the frame; the frame reacts to it.

## Notes for AI

- Never wrap `input` in this group to "add a border"; the input already has one.
- Put state on `InputGroupInput` (`aria-invalid`, `disabled`, `readOnly`) — the frame is
  chrome, and it inherits the appearance.
- Use `InputGroupButton`, not `Button`, inside the frame: the sizes are on the addon
  scale, and the addon's click handler recognises it as a button.

# Breadcrumb

The trail from the root to the current page.

## When to use

- A hierarchy deeper than two levels, where the user needs to know where they are and
  how to get back up: `Workspace / Projects / cadence-ui`.
- A page reached through a drill-down — a file inside a folder inside a drive.
- A trail that doubles as navigation: every ancestor is a link, the current page is
  not.

## When not to use

- Two levels of depth. The header already links home; a trail of two items adds noise.
- A wizard or a multi-step form. That is a progress indicator, and it must not let the
  user jump to a step they have not reached.
- A history of where the user came from ("back to search results"). That is a back
  link, and it should look like one.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/breadcrumb
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@/components/cadence/breadcrumb/breadcrumb";

export function Trail() {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>plan.pdf</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### A deep trail that collapses

`BreadcrumbEllipsis` stands in for the middle of a long path. Put a menu trigger next
to it — the ellipsis itself is not interactive.

```tsx
<BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
</BreadcrumbItem>
<BreadcrumbSeparator />
```

### A custom separator

`BreadcrumbSeparator` takes any child; without one it renders a chevron at `size-3.5`.

```tsx
<BreadcrumbSeparator>
  <span className="text-muted-foreground/60">/</span>
</BreadcrumbSeparator>
```

### A router link

`BreadcrumbLink` takes Base UI's `render`, so the framework's own link component keeps
its prefetching and client-side navigation. The `data-slot` survives the swap.

```tsx
<BreadcrumbLink render={<Link href="/files" />}>Files</BreadcrumbLink>
```

## API

| Part                   | Props                 | Notes                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Breadcrumb`           | native nav props      | `aria-label="breadcrumb"`.                                    |
| `BreadcrumbList`       | native ol props       | Flex row that wraps; muted, small text.                       |
| `BreadcrumbItem`       | native li props       | Inline flex, one gap.                                         |
| `BreadcrumbLink`       | `render`, anchor props| Anchor by default; `data-slot="breadcrumb-link"`.             |
| `BreadcrumbPage`       | native span props     | The current page: `aria-current="page"`, not a link.          |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator`  | native li props       | `role="presentation"`, `aria-hidden`; chevron by default.     |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis`   | native span props     | Hidden from assistive tech; contains `sr-only` "More".        |

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). Nothing in a trail animates. A navigation landmark that fades or
slides in is harder to find, and a trail that reflows on navigation makes the one
stable thing on the page move.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

`transition-colors` on the link is hover feedback on the text colour only.

## Accessibility

- The `nav` is labelled "breadcrumb", so it becomes its own landmark; a page may have
  several `nav`s and this is how they are told apart.
- Order matters: `<ol>`/`<li>` gives the trail a length and a sequence, which is what
  a screen reader announces ("list, 3 items").
- The last item is `BreadcrumbPage`: `aria-current="page"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and
  not focusable. It is where the user already is, so linking it is a no-op that costs a
  tab stop.
- Separators are decorative — `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden` — so the trail is
  read as names, not as "chevron".
- An ellipsis must not be the only way to reach the hidden ancestors: pair it with a
  menu, or the collapsed path becomes unreachable.

## Notes for AI

- Do not wrap the current page in a link "for consistency". It is a `BreadcrumbPage`.
- Do not put the trail in a `Card` header as decoration; it is navigation and belongs
  near the top of the content region.
- If the hierarchy is generated from a route, derive the trail from the route's
  segments rather than hand-writing items — a trail that disagrees with the URL is
  worse than none.

# Pagination

Page navigation that stays a link, not a button.

## When to use

- A result set that is paged for a reason: the total is unknown, the data is remote, or
  the URL should carry the page so it can be shared and reloaded.
- A list where the user needs to jump to a specific page, not only step forward.
- A table footer on the server, where the count lives in the response.

## When not to use

- A finite list that is already in memory. Render it, or a "load more" button — paging
  something you already have is a worse experience than scrolling.
- An infinite feed. There is no page to link to, so an anchor-based control lies.
- A carousel or a wizard. Those step through slides or steps, and their controls are
  buttons.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/pagination
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@/components/cadence/pagination/pagination";

export function Pages({ page }: { page: number }) {
  return (
    <Pagination>
      <PaginationContent>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationPrevious href={`?page=${page - 1}`} />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationLink href="?page=1" isActive={page === 1}>
            1
          </PaginationLink>
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem>
          <PaginationNext href={`?page=${page + 1}`} />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### A collapsed range

`PaginationEllipsis` marks the pages that are not rendered. It is hidden from
assistive tech, so the list stays short for a screen reader too.

```tsx
<PaginationItem>
  <PaginationEllipsis />
</PaginationItem>
```

### Custom labels

`PaginationPrevious` and `PaginationNext` take `text`; the label is hidden below `sm`,
where the chevron carries the meaning and the accessible name still says "Go to
previous page".

```tsx
<PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" text="Back" />
<PaginationNext href="?page=3" text="Forward" />
```

### Without a page in the URL

Keep the anchor and intercept the click; do not swap it for a button. The anchor keeps
middle-click, copy-link, and the "link" announcement.

```tsx
<PaginationLink
  href="#"
  onClick={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    setPage(3);
  }}
>
  3
</PaginationLink>
```

## API

| Part                  | Props                    | Notes                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Pagination`          | native nav props         | `aria-label="pagination"`, `role="navigation"`.                |
| `PaginationContent`   | native ul props          | Row with a one-unit gap.                                       |
| `PaginationItem`      | native li props          | One slot in the list.                                          |
| `PaginationLink`      | `isActive`, `size`, anchors | Always an `<a>`; `aria-current="page"` and `data-active` when active. |
| `PaginationPrevious`  | `text`, link props       | Chevron left; `aria-label="Go to previous page"`.              |
| `PaginationNext`      | `text`, link props       | Chevron right; `aria-label="Go to next page"`.                 |
| `PaginationEllipsis`  | native span props        | `aria-hidden`; contains `sr-only` "More pages".                |

`size` comes from the button variants (`icon` by default), so the shape matches a
button without becoming one.

## Motion contract

No motion (T0). A page change is a navigation: the content that changes is the list,
not the control. Animating the pagination would animate the one thing that stays the
same.

| Phase   | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| –       | none       | –     | –             |
| reduced | none       | –     | –             |
| none    | none       | –     | –             |

If the new page's rows should arrive in sequence, that is `list.stagger` on the list.

## Accessibility

- `aria-label="pagination"` names the landmark, so it can be skipped or listed.
- The current page is `aria-current="page"`. Colour and the outline variant are the
  sighted half of the same signal — never the only one.
- Previous and next carry a written `aria-label`, because their visible text is hidden
  below `sm`. The chevron alone is not a name.
- A disabled end state (`page 1`, no previous) should render the control without an
  `href` and with `aria-disabled="true"`, not a link that 404s.
- The ordered list gives the count; the ellipsis is decorative and must not be
  focusable.

## Notes for AI

- Every control is an anchor. Do not replace it with `Button` — the shape comes from
  `buttonVariants`, and Base UI's button would put `role="button"` on a link.
- Keep `href` real (`?page=3`) even when a click handler takes over: it is what makes
  the control shareable and middle-clickable.
- Do not render more than about seven items; collapse the middle with
  `PaginationEllipsis`.

# Spinner

An indeterminate wait, rotating until the work finishes.

## When to use

- An action the user just triggered: save, send, invite, publish. The spinner sits
  where the user is looking — inside the button, or immediately beside it.
- A wait with no measurable progress: a request that returns when it returns.
- A region that is loading and whose shape you cannot predict. When you *can* predict
  it, use `skeleton` instead: it keeps the layout stable.

## When not to use

- A wait under about 300 ms. The spinner appears and disappears before it can be read,
  which reads as a flicker. Keep the button's label and disable it.
- A known percentage. Use `progress`; a spinning wheel after "60%" is a regression.
- A page that is loading its first paint. There is nothing to spin inside yet — a
  skeleton or a server-rendered shell is better.
- A decorative "we're working on it" on a marketing page. Motion without a state
  change is decoration (P9).

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/spinner
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner/spinner";

export function LoadingRegistry() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3 text-sm">
      <Spinner />
      <span className="text-muted-foreground">Loading the registry…</span>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Inside a button

The button keeps its width because the spinner replaces nothing: keep the label and
put the spinner in front of it, or reserve the label's space with `aria-live`.

```tsx
<Button disabled size="sm">
  <Spinner />
  Saving
</Button>
```

### Sized by the caller

The icon is `size-4` by default and inherits `currentColor`, so one class resizes and
recolours it.

```tsx
<Spinner className="size-3 text-muted-foreground" />
```

### A specific label

"Loading" is the default. Say what is loading when the surrounding text does not.

```tsx
<Spinner aria-label="Saving invoice" />
```

### Under `data-motion="none"`

The rotation stops; the icon stays and the label still says "Loading". A stopped
spinner is still a state, which is why `none` does not remove it from the tree.

```tsx
<CadenceProvider mode="none">
  <Spinner />
</CadenceProvider>
```

## API

| Prop        | Type     | Default     | Description                                                    |
| ----------- | -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | –           | Merged last — size and colour live here (`size-3`, `text-…`).   |
| `aria-label`| `string` | `"Loading"` | The accessible name; pass a specific one when it helps.         |

All native `svg` props are forwarded. `data-slot="spinner"` and `data-motion` are
always set, and `role="status"` with the label is the announcement.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `data.transition`, continuous form. The loop is CSS (`animate-spin`) rather
than Motion, for the same reason as `skeleton`: a spinner is by definition next to work
the user is waiting on, and it must not add a frame callback to it. Only `transform`
(rotation) changes, so the loop can never trigger layout.

| Phase   | Properties          | Token                         | Interruptible |
| ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------- |
| spin    | `rotate 0 → 360deg` | `animate-spin` (theme timing) | yes (CSS)     |
| reduced | same rotation       | `animate-spin`                | yes (CSS)     |
| none    | none; icon static   | `animate-none`                | –             |

Reduced keeps the rotation on purpose: M5 removes travel and scale, and a rotation in
place is neither. A spinner that freezes under reduced motion would read as a frozen
app. `none` stops it completely, which is what a screenshot test or a print stylesheet
needs.

## Keyboard interactions

None. The spinner is not focusable and takes no input; focus stays on the control that
started the work, which is where the user's next action will be.

## Accessibility

- `role="status"` is a polite live region: the label is announced when the spinner
  appears, without interrupting. Do not wrap it in another `aria-live` region.
- The label must carry the meaning. The rotation is never the only signal, and under
  `data-motion="none"` it is not a signal at all.
- Give the busy region `aria-busy="true"` and remove it when the work finishes, so the
  state survives even if the spinner unmounts early.
- Do not replace a button's label with a spinner and nothing else. Keep the word, or
  add an `sr-only` copy, or the control loses its name mid-action.
- Do not stack spinners. One per action; a page with five is a page with no feedback.

## Responsive behavior

The spinner is an inline icon, so it follows the text it sits in. Inside a button it
keeps the button's height; inside a heading, size it down (`size-3`) or it will
dominate the line. On touch targets, keep the surrounding button at least 44×44 by
size, not by growing the icon.

## Performance

- One CSS animation per element, on `transform` only; no JS loop, no layout read.
- Compositor-friendly, but the animation-system budget still applies: fewer than
  twenty simultaneously animating elements. For a list of pending rows, render one
  spinner for the list, not one per row.
- No `will-change`: the browser promotes a transform animation on its own.

## Notes for AI

- Use `spinner` for an action, `skeleton` for a layout. Getting this backwards is the
  most common loading-state mistake: a skeleton in a button, or a spinner where the
  content shape was known all along.
- Keep the button's text; add the spinner in front of it and disable the button.
- Under `data-motion="none"` the icon stays visible. Do not hide it to "respect" the
  preference — the state still has to be visible.

# Dialog

A modal window that fades and settles in, with the open and close sequence interruptible.

## When to use

- A focused task that must interrupt the page: rename, invite, confirm.
- Content that needs a modal, a focus trap, and an obvious escape route.
- A short form whose result matters more than the page behind it.

## When not to use

- Non-blocking hints and menus; use `popover` or `tooltip`.
- Long multi-step flows; use a page or a wizard.
- Mobile sheets with drag gestures; use `drawer`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the dialog uses for its close control.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/dialog/dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <Dialog>
      <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete project</DialogTrigger>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle>Delete this project?</DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription>This removes every deployment and cannot be undone.</DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>
        <DialogFooter>
          <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
          <Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
        </DialogFooter>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DialogContent>…</DialogContent>
</Dialog>;
```

### Without the built-in close button

```tsx
<DialogContent showCloseButton={false}>…</DialogContent>
```

### Footer with a close action

```tsx
<DialogFooter showCloseButton>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</DialogFooter>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. |
| `DialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `DialogContent` | `showCloseButton`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `DialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `DialogContent`. |
| `DialogClose` | native button props, `render` | Closes the dialog. |
| `DialogHeader` / `DialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `DialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `DialogDescription` | `className` | Optional supporting text. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The panel stays mounted while its exit transition runs; Base UI delays unmount until the
transition ends, so reopening mid-exit reverses cleanly.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. |
| Escape | Closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused control. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`,
  focus trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and Escape handling.
- The close button is a real button with a screen-reader-only label.
- `DialogTitle` is required; a dialog without an accessible name is invalid.
- Content is unmounted after the exit transition, so focus is never lost mid-flight.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred and capped at `max-w-lg`; on narrow viewports it keeps a 1rem gutter.
Long content scrolls inside the popup rather than the page.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open.
- Animates opacity and scale only; no layout reads and no JavaScript animation loop.

## Notes for AI

- Always render a `DialogTitle`; it is the accessible name.
- Keep the confirming action specific ("Delete project", not "OK").
- Do not animate height inside the dialog; mount content instead.

# Checkbox

A control that allows the user to toggle between checked and not checked.

## When to use

- One independent yes/no choice: accept the terms, remember this device, include
  archived items.
- A set of choices where several can be true at once; use one checkbox per row.
- A parent row that summarises children: pass `indeterminate` while the children
  disagree.
- A table row selection, where each row is its own decision.

## When not to use

- Exactly one of several options; use `radio-group`, which also gives arrow-key
  navigation.
- An immediate setting that applies the moment it is flipped; use `switch`.
- A formatting command that acts on a selection; use `toggle`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/checkbox
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@/components/cadence/checkbox/checkbox";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label";

export function Terms() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-start gap-3">
      <Checkbox id="terms" />
      <Label htmlFor="terms">Accept the terms of service</Label>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`id` lands on the hidden input, so `htmlFor` on a `label` names the control and
clicking the label toggles it.

## Examples

### Checked by default, and indeterminate

```tsx
<Checkbox defaultChecked />
<Checkbox indeterminate />
```

`indeterminate` is a visual third state; `aria-checked="mixed"` is what a screen
reader hears. It never replaces the checked state — pass `checked` too if the
form needs a value.

### Controlled

```tsx
const [accepted, setAccepted] = useState(false);

<Checkbox checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} />;
```

### Invalid, with a described error

```tsx
<Checkbox id="terms" aria-invalid aria-describedby="terms-error" />
<p id="terms-error" className="text-sm text-destructive">
  You must accept the terms to continue.
</p>
```

The ring turns destructive because `aria-invalid` is set. The component does not
decide that anything is wrong.

### In a row of settings

```tsx
<div className="flex items-start gap-3">
  <Checkbox id="digest" className="mt-0.5" />
  <div className="grid gap-1">
    <Label htmlFor="digest">Send the weekly digest</Label>
    <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Every Monday, 09:00.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## API

| Prop               | Type                              | Default | Description                                          |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`          | `boolean`                         | –       | Controlled state.                                    |
| `defaultChecked`   | `boolean`                         | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state.                          |
| `onCheckedChange`  | `(checked, details) => void`      | –       | Fired on click and on Space.                         |
| `indeterminate`    | `boolean`                         | `false` | Mixed visual state for a parent row.                 |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                         | `false` | Ignores interaction and form submission.             |
| `readOnly`         | `boolean`                         | `false` | Focusable, submitted, not changeable.                |
| `required`         | `boolean`                         | `false` | Blocks form submission until checked.                |
| `name`, `value`    | `string`                          | –       | Form field identity and submitted value.             |
| `className`        | `string`                          | –       | Merged last.                                         |

All native attributes are forwarded, including `aria-invalid` and
`aria-describedby`.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. The tick is the protagonist — it fades in and settles from
0.96 to full size when the box is checked, and reverses when it is cleared.

| Phase   | Properties                    | Token          | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| check   | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes (re-click) |
| clear   | the same pair, reversed       | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| reduced | `opacity` only                | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| none    | no transition                 | –              | –             |

Only the indicator moves. The box itself keeps a `transition-shadow` for the focus
ring and the invalid ring, which is colour/shadow state feedback, not motion.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys          | Action                                     |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `Tab`         | Moves focus to the checkbox.               |
| `Space`       | Toggles checked, unless `readOnly`.        |
| `Shift+Tab`   | Moves focus to the previous control.       |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders `role="checkbox"` on the visible element plus a hidden
  `<input type="checkbox">`, so the control is in the form and in the tab order.
- The tick is not the announcement: the state lives in `aria-checked`, which is
  why the reduced and `none` branches stay usable.
- Always pair the box with a `Label` (`htmlFor`) or an `aria-label`; a bare box
  has no accessible name.
- `indeterminate` announces as "mixed". Do not use it as a substitute for
  `checked` in a form.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                  | You do                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid` and forwards it to the input   | Deciding whether the box must be checked             |
| Forwards `required`, `name`, `value`, `disabled`     | Building the submitted payload                       |
| Announces `aria-checked` for all three states        | Mapping the error to the field with `aria-describedby` |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

The control is fixed at 16px with a 44px touch target (the `after:` pseudo
element extends the hit area), so it behaves the same at every breakpoint. Put the
label beside it, not inside it; wrapping a checkbox in a label removes the
`aria-describedby` chain.

## Performance

No JS animation loop: one Motion element per box, animating only `opacity` and
`transform`. A list of 50 checkboxes is 50 short transitions on demand, never a
running loop.

## Notes for AI

- Use `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` for errors; there is no `error` prop.
- Do not add press animation to a checkbox; the tick is the only protagonist.
- For "one of N", use `radio-group`; for an instant setting, use `switch`.

# Radio Group

A set of checkable buttons where no more than one can be checked at a time.

## When to use

- A small, fixed set of options where exactly one applies: a plan, a priority, a
  shipping method.
- Anywhere seeing all the options at once matters more than saving space.
- A setting that applies on submit, not immediately.

## When not to use

- Several answers can be true; use `checkbox`.
- The setting applies the moment it changes; use `switch`.
- More than about seven options, or a list that is filtered as you type; use
  `select` or `combobox`, which handle long lists and search.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/radio-group
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/radio-group/radio-group";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label";

export function Plan() {
  return (
    <RadioGroup defaultValue="team" aria-label="Plan">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <RadioGroupItem id="plan-team" value="team" />
        <Label htmlFor="plan-team">Team</Label>
      </div>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <RadioGroupItem id="plan-scale" value="scale" />
        <Label htmlFor="plan-scale">Scale</Label>
      </div>
    </RadioGroup>
  );
}
```

Every item needs a `value`. The group is one form field: `name` goes on the
group, not on the items.

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
const [plan, setPlan] = useState("team");

<RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan} aria-label="Plan">
  …
</RadioGroup>;
```

`onValueChange` receives the new value plus Base UI's event details.

### Invalid

```tsx
<RadioGroup aria-invalid aria-describedby="plan-error" aria-label="Plan">
  …
</RadioGroup>
<p id="plan-error" className="text-sm text-destructive">
  Choose a plan to continue.
</p>
```

`aria-invalid` on the group styles the items and is announced with the group.

### Disabled item

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="starter" aria-label="Plan">
  <RadioGroupItem value="starter" id="p1" />
  <RadioGroupItem value="enterprise" id="p2" disabled />
</RadioGroup>
```

A disabled item is still visible and still announced, so the option does not
appear to vanish.

## API

### `RadioGroup`

| Prop            | Type                                          | Default | Description                                     |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `string`                                      | –       | Controlled selection.                           |
| `defaultValue`  | `string`                                      | –       | Uncontrolled initial selection.                 |
| `onValueChange` | `(value, details) => void`                    | –       | Fired when the selection changes.               |
| `name`          | `string`                                      | –       | Form field name, submitted with the selection.  |
| `disabled`      | `boolean`                                     | `false` | Disables every item.                            |
| `required`      | `boolean`                                     | `false` | Blocks submit until something is selected.      |
| `className`     | `string`                                      | –       | Merged last; the default is `grid gap-3`.       |

### `RadioGroupItem`

| Prop        | Type      | Default | Description                              |
| ----------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `value`     | `string`  | –       | Required. Identifies this option.        |
| `disabled`  | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the option visible but unselectable.|
| `className` | `string`  | –       | Merged last.                             |

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. The dot of the newly selected item fades in and settles
from 0.96 to full size; the previously selected dot reverses. Nothing else in the
row moves, so the eye follows the choice.

| Phase     | Properties                        | Token          | Interruptible |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| select    | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| deselect  | the same pair, reversed           | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| reduced   | `opacity` only                    | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| none      | no transition                     | –              | –             |

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                | Action                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`               | Enters the group at the selected item (or the first one).     |
| `Arrow Right/Down`  | Selects the next item and moves focus.                        |
| `Arrow Left/Up`     | Selects the previous item and moves focus.                    |
| `Space`             | Selects the focused item.                                     |

There is one tab stop for the whole group, not one per item: that is the roving
tabindex Base UI implements.

## Accessibility

- The group renders `role="radiogroup"`; each item renders `role="radio"` with a
  hidden input, so the form still submits a value.
- `aria-checked` carries the state on its own. The dot animation is never the only
  signal.
- Name the group with `aria-labelledby` pointing at a visible heading, or with
  `aria-label` when a heading would be redundant.
- `aria-invalid` belongs on the group: it describes the whole choice.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                 | You do                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles and announces `aria-invalid` on the group   | Deciding that a choice is required                |
| Forwards `name`, `required`, and the selection      | Server-side validation of the submitted value     |
| Keeps arrow-key navigation within the group         | Focus policy after a failed submit                |

There is no `validate` or `schema` prop. See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

Items stack by default (`grid gap-3`). For a horizontal row of short labels, set
`className="flex flex-wrap gap-6"`; do not shorten the labels to fit — wrap them.

## Performance

One Motion element per item, each animating only `opacity` and `transform`, and
only when the selection changes. No layout thrash: the dot is absolutely sized by
CSS, so no measurement happens.

## Notes for AI

- Use `radio-group` for "one of N" and `checkbox` for "any of N".
- Put `name` and `aria-invalid` on the group, not on the items.
- Do not build a radio group out of buttons with `aria-pressed`; the radio role
  is what gives arrow-key navigation and form submission.

# Switch

A control that toggles between on and off, with a thumb that travels between the two states.

## When to use

- A setting that takes effect immediately: public/private, alerts on/off, a feature
  flag.
- A row in a settings list, where the label describes the thing and the switch
  describes its state.
- A preference with no submit button. Flipping it saves.

## When not to use

- The change is only applied on submit; use `checkbox`, which is the familiar form
  control for a pending decision.
- One of several options; use `radio-group`.
- A formatting command on a selection; use `toggle`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/switch
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch/switch";
import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label";

export function Public() {
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
      <Label htmlFor="public">Public workspace</Label>
      <Switch id="public" defaultChecked />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Sizes

```tsx
<Switch defaultChecked />
<Switch size="sm" defaultChecked />
```

`size="sm"` keeps the same travel logic: the distance is measured from the track
and the thumb, so restyling either keeps the end position correct.

### Controlled

```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(false);

<Switch checked={on} onCheckedChange={setOn} aria-label="Alerts" />;
```

### In a settings row

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
  <div className="grid gap-1">
    <Label htmlFor="alerts">Deploy alerts</Label>
    <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">A notification for every failed build.</p>
  </div>
  <Switch id="alerts" />
</div>
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<Switch disabled defaultChecked />
```

Disabled switches stay visible and announced; hiding them loses the information
that the setting exists.

## API

| Prop              | Type                        | Default     | Description                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `checked`         | `boolean`                   | –           | Controlled state.                              |
| `defaultChecked`  | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Uncontrolled initial state.                    |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked, details) => void`| –           | Fired on click and on Space.                   |
| `size`            | `"sm" \| "default"`         | `"default"` | Track and thumb scale.                         |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Ignores interaction and form submission.       |
| `readOnly`        | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Focusable, submitted, not changeable.          |
| `required`        | `boolean`                   | `false`     | Blocks submit until switched on.               |
| `name`, `value`   | `string`                    | –           | Form field identity and submitted value.       |
| `className`       | `string`                    | –           | Merged last.                                   |

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. The thumb travels from one end of the track to the other
while the track recolours. The travel distance is measured from the rendered track
and thumb — no hard-coded pixel value — so a custom size still lands flush.

| Phase   | Properties                         | Token          | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| on      | `translateX 0 → track − thumb`     | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| off     | the same distance, reversed        | `state.morph`  | yes           |
| reduced | no travel animation; the thumb jumps to the new end | – | –     |
| none    | no transition                      | –              | –             |

Under `reduced` the thumb still ends up in the right place: position is state, not
decoration. What is dropped is the animation, so the movement is instant.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys    | Action                                  |
| ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves focus to the switch.              |
| `Space` | Toggles the switch, unless `readOnly`.  |
| `Enter` | Does not toggle — that is native button behaviour, and a switch is not a button. |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders `role="switch"` with `aria-checked` and a hidden input, so the
  value is submitted with the form.
- The state is not carried by colour alone: the thumb position, the track colour,
  and `aria-checked` change together.
- Give it a name with `Label htmlFor` or `aria-label`. "On" is a state, not a name.
- A switch that saves immediately should announce the outcome (a `toast` or an
  inline status), because there is no submit step to confirm it.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                              | You do                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Forwards `name`, `value`, `disabled`, `required` | Persisting the setting and handling failures     |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling                   | Deciding whether the switch needs one at all     |
| Renders the on/off state                         | Announcing that the change was saved             |

There is no `validate` or `schema` prop. See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

The control is fixed-size at every breakpoint; the row around it is what changes.
In a narrow layout, let the label and description wrap above the switch instead of
shrinking the track.

## Performance

One `ResizeObserver` per switch measures the travel, so a font or layout change
does not desynchronise the thumb. The animation itself is a single `transform`
transition with no layout reads during interaction.

## Notes for AI

- Use `switch` only for immediate settings. If there is a Save button, use
  `checkbox`.
- Do not animate the track colour as motion; colour is state feedback.
- Keep the label outside the switch. A switch with no label has no accessible name.

# Slider

An input where the user selects a value from a range by dragging a thumb.

## When to use

- A value where the rough position matters more than the exact number: volume,
  brightness, zoom, opacity.
- A range (two thumbs): price between, time window, budget band.
- A filter where the user should feel the bounds instead of typing them.

## When not to use

- An exact number matters and the range is wide; pair a `slider` with an `input`,
  or use `input` alone.
- Fewer than about five discrete options; use `radio-group` or `toggle-group`.
- A value with no natural order, like picking a colour name.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/slider
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@/components/cadence/slider/slider";

export function Volume() {
  return <Slider defaultValue={[60]} max={100} aria-label="Volume" />;
}
```

`defaultValue` and `value` are always arrays: one entry per thumb. `aria-label`
on the slider is forwarded to every thumb's native range input, which is what a
screen reader announces. A range slider gets one accessible name per thumb —
`Price (minimum)` and `Price (maximum)` — because two inputs with the same name
are indistinguishable.

## Examples

### Controlled

```tsx
const [volume, setVolume] = useState([60]);

<Slider value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} aria-label="Volume" />;
```

### Range

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[120, 480]} min={0} max={600} step={10} aria-label="Price" />
```

Two entries in the array give two thumbs; `minStepsBetweenValues` keeps them from
crossing.

### Vertical

```tsx
<Slider orientation="vertical" defaultValue={[40]} className="h-56" aria-label="Level" />
```

Give the vertical slider a height; the track fills it.

### Disabled

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[40]} disabled aria-label="Volume" />
```

## API

| Prop                 | Type                              | Default        | Description                                     |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `value`              | `number \| readonly number[]`     | –              | Controlled value, one entry per thumb.          |
| `defaultValue`       | same as `value`                   | –              | Uncontrolled initial value.                     |
| `onValueChange`      | `(value, details) => void`        | –              | Fired while dragging and on keyboard steps.     |
| `min`, `max`         | `number`                          | `0`, `100`     | Bounds.                                         |
| `step`               | `number`                          | `1`            | Snap increment.                                 |
| `orientation`        | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`      | `"horizontal"` | Axis.                                           |
| `disabled`           | `boolean`                         | `false`        | Ignores pointer and keyboard.                   |
| `aria-label`         | `string`                          | –              | Forwarded to each thumb, suffixed per thumb.    |
| `className`          | `string`                          | –              | Merged last.                                    |

Base UI's `format`, `locale`, and `minStepsBetweenValues` are forwarded unchanged.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`. The dragged thumb compresses to 0.97 and springs back on
release — the same press language as `button` and `toggle`.

| Phase   | Properties              | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ----------------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| drag    | `scale 1 → 0.97`        | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1`        | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the ring grows on focus/hover | – | –             |
| none    | no scale                | –                | –             |

The fill is deliberately not animated: it is glued to the pointer, and a
transition would make it trail the thumb by one frame per move.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys                | Action                                  |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`               | Moves focus to the thumb.               |
| `Arrow Right/Up`    | Increases by one `step`.                |
| `Arrow Left/Down`   | Decreases by one `step`.                |
| `Page Up`/`Page Down` | Moves by a larger increment.           |
| `Home`/`End`        | Jumps to `min` / `max`.                 |

## Accessibility

- Every thumb contains a native `input[type=range]`, so the control works with
  assistive technology without a custom role.
- Always pass `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) — the fill has no text.
- Show the current value as text next to the slider when the number matters.
  Dragging is not a way to read a value.
- `aria-invalid` styles the control; validation is the caller's job (P11).

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                | You do                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Reports the value through `onValueChange`         | Deciding whether the range is acceptable            |
| Styles `aria-invalid`                             | Writing the error text and its `aria-describedby` id |
| Steps and clamps the value to `min`/`max`         | Server-side bounds and business rules               |

See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

Horizontal sliders fill their container (`w-full`); vertical ones fill their
height. On touch screens the thumb keeps a 16px visual size but the range input
covers the whole control, so drag targets stay reachable.

## Performance

The value updates on pointer move without React re-rendering the whole form: Base
UI moves the thumb with a CSS custom property, and Motion animates only the press
scale. No `layout` animation, no measurement per frame.

## Notes for AI

- Values are arrays. `value={50}` is a type error; use `value={[50]}`.
- Do not animate the fill. Motion here is press feedback only.
- Pair with an `input` when the exact number must be typeable.

# Toggle

A two-state button that can be pressed or not pressed.

## When to use

- A formatting or mode command that stays on until it is turned off: bold,
  italic, a preview pane, a grid/list switch.
- A compact toolbar button whose pressed state is visible next to its neighbours.
- A setting the user toggles repeatedly while working.

## When not to use

- The action is one-shot (save, delete, open); use `button`.
- A setting that takes effect immediately and permanently, like a preference; use
  `switch`.
- A group of related toggles that should read as one control; use `toggle-group`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Bold } from "lucide-react";
import { Toggle } from "@/components/cadence/toggle/toggle";

export function BoldToggle() {
  return (
    <Toggle aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed>
      <Bold />
    </Toggle>
  );
}
```

An icon-only toggle needs `aria-label`; the glyph is not a name.

## Examples

### Variants and sizes

```tsx
<Toggle>Default</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="outline">Outline</Toggle>

<Toggle size="sm">Small</Toggle>
<Toggle size="lg">Large</Toggle>
```

`outline` gives the toggle a border, for toolbars that sit on a busy surface.

### With a label

```tsx
<Toggle variant="outline">
  <Bold />
  Bold
</Toggle>
```

`gap-2` is already in the base classes, so an icon and a label space themselves.

### Controlled

```tsx
const [on, setOn] = useState(false);

<Toggle pressed={on} onPressedChange={setOn} aria-label="Bold" />;
```

### Inside a form

```tsx
<Toggle name="bold" defaultPressed value="bold" />
```

A pressed toggle submits its `value`; an unpressed one submits nothing, like a
checkbox.

## API

| Prop               | Type                          | Default     | Description                              |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `pressed`          | `boolean`                     | –           | Controlled state.                        |
| `defaultPressed`   | `boolean`                     | `false`     | Uncontrolled initial state.              |
| `onPressedChange`  | `(pressed, details) => void`  | –           | Fired on click and on Space/Enter.       |
| `variant`          | `"default" \| "outline"`      | `"default"` | Visual weight.                           |
| `size`             | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`   | `"default"` | Height and minimum width.                |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                     | `false`     | Ignores interaction.                     |
| `className`        | `string`                      | –           | Merged last.                             |

`toggleVariants` is exported, so a custom part can share the same classes.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`. The button compresses to 0.97 while the pointer is down
and springs back on release.

| Phase   | Properties       | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| press   | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the pressed background is the only change | – | – |
| none    | no scale         | –                | –             |

The pressed background is a colour transition, which is state feedback and stays
in every mode — otherwise a `none` user could not see the state.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys    | Action                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `Tab`   | Moves focus to the toggle.      |
| `Space` | Toggles the pressed state.      |
| `Enter` | Toggles the pressed state.      |

## Accessibility

- Base UI renders a real `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed`, so assistive
  technology announces it as a toggle button, not a plain button.
- Icon-only toggles need `aria-label`; the pressed state is announced separately.
- The pressed state is never colour-only: the fill and `aria-pressed` change
  together, and the press scale is never the only feedback.
- Avoid toggles in a navigation bar; a link that changes style is still a link.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                            | You do                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Forwards `name`, `value`, `disabled`          | Deciding what a pressed toggle means       |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling                | Validation and error text                  |
| Keeps the pressed state in `aria-pressed`     | Persisting it                              |

See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

Sizes are fixed; in a toolbar that must shrink, drop to `size="sm"` rather than
scaling the button with a transform, which would blur the icon.

## Performance

One Motion element, pressing only on pointer down. No layout animation, no
measurement.

## Notes for AI

- Use `toggle` for a command that stays on; use `switch` for a preference that
  saves itself.
- Always provide `aria-label` for icon-only toggles.
- Do not add a `state.morph` label swap to a toggle; the press scale is the whole
  contract.

# Toggle Group

A set of two-state buttons that can be pressed one at a time or together.

## When to use

- A small set of modes that belong to one control: text alignment, view density,
  a time range.
- A formatting toolbar where several marks can be active at once
  (`multiple`).
- Anywhere the options are icons and the choice should read as one segmented
  control (`spacing={0}` + `variant="outline"`).

## When not to use

- Exactly one option with a text label and a longer list; use `radio-group`, which
  exposes radio semantics rather than a row of toggle buttons.
- A single independent on/off command; use `toggle`.
- Navigation between pages; use `tabs`, which owns `role="tablist"`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/toggle-group
```

Installing the group also installs `toggle`, because the items share its variant
classes.

## Usage

```tsx
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight } from "lucide-react";
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "@/components/cadence/toggle-group/toggle-group";

export function Alignment() {
  return (
    <ToggleGroup variant="outline" defaultValue={["left"]} aria-label="Text alignment">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
        <AlignRight />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Multiple

```tsx
<ToggleGroup multiple defaultValue={["bold"]} aria-label="Text style">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
    <Bold />
  </ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
    <Italic />
  </ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

Without `multiple`, pressing an item releases the others.

### Spacing

```tsx
<ToggleGroup variant="outline" spacing={0} aria-label="Range">
  …
</ToggleGroup>

<ToggleGroup variant="outline" spacing={1} aria-label="Range">
  …
</ToggleGroup>
```

`spacing={0}` joins the borders into one segmented control; a positive value
keeps the items apart in Tailwind spacing steps.

### Vertical

```tsx
<ToggleGroup orientation="vertical" aria-label="Zoom">
  …
</ToggleGroup>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(["center"]);

<ToggleGroup value={value} onValueChange={setValue} aria-label="Alignment">
  …
</ToggleGroup>;
```

The value is always an array, even without `multiple`.

## API

### `ToggleGroup`

| Prop            | Type                                        | Default        | Description                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `value`         | `readonly string[]`                         | –              | Controlled pressed values.               |
| `defaultValue`  | `readonly string[]`                         | `[]`           | Uncontrolled initial values.             |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[], details) => void`        | –              | Fired when any item changes.             |
| `multiple`      | `boolean`                                   | `false`        | Allow more than one pressed item.        |
| `spacing`       | `number`                                    | `0`            | Gap in Tailwind spacing steps.           |
| `orientation`   | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"`                | `"horizontal"` | Axis, also drives arrow keys.            |
| `variant`       | `"default" \| "outline"`                    | `"default"`    | Inherited by every item.                 |
| `size`          | `"sm" \| "default" \| "lg"`                 | `"default"`    | Inherited by every item.                 |

### `ToggleGroupItem`

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `value`     | `string` | –       | Required. Identifies the item.       |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`| `false` | Keeps it visible but unpressable.    |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last.                         |

## Motion contract

Recipe: `feedback.press`, inherited by every item — pressing compresses that item
and springs it back, exactly like a standalone `toggle`.

| Phase   | Properties       | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------- |
| press   | `scale 1 → 0.97` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| release | `scale 0.97 → 1` | `feedback.press` | yes           |
| reduced | no scale; the pressed background carries the state | – | – |
| none    | no scale         | –                | –             |

The group itself does not animate. A shared sliding indicator would need the
pressed item to change size, which would move the neighbours the user is aiming
at — a T3 concern, not a press.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys               | Action                                        |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`              | Enters the group at the last pressed item.    |
| `Arrow Right/Down` | Moves focus to the next item.                 |
| `Arrow Left/Up`    | Moves focus to the previous item.             |
| `Space` / `Enter`  | Presses the focused item.                     |

With `loopFocus` (default) the arrows wrap around at the ends.

## Accessibility

- The group renders `role="group"`; each item is a `<button>` with `aria-pressed`.
- Name the group with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` — a row of icon buttons
  with no group name is announced as unrelated buttons.
- Icon-only items need their own `aria-label`; the group name does not describe
  them.
- Do not use a toggle group where `role="tablist"` is correct; tabs imply a panel
  that is shown, a toggle group implies state.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                              | You do                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Forwards `disabled` and the pressed values      | Deciding whether a selection is required  |
| Renders the visual pressed state                | Persisting the choice                     |
| Exposes `aria-invalid` styling on items         | Validation and error text                 |

See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

Horizontal groups do not wrap; with more than about five items on a narrow screen,
switch to `orientation="vertical"` or replace the group with a `select`.

## Performance

One Motion element per item, pressing on demand. No layout animation and no
measurement, so a group of eight items costs nothing until one is pressed.

## Notes for AI

- `value` is an array in every mode, with or without `multiple`.
- Use `spacing={0}` + `variant="outline"` for a segmented control.
- For "one of N" with text labels, prefer `radio-group`; for panels, `tabs`.

# Input OTP

A one-time password field that renders one slot per character.

## When to use

- A short code the user reads from another surface: a login code, an email
  verification, a device pairing code.
- Anywhere a single input would force the user to count characters.
- A code that arrives by SMS or authenticator app, where `autocomplete="one-time-code"`
  lets the OS offer it.

## When not to use

- A password the user chooses; use `input type="password"`.
- A long token that is pasted, not typed; use `input` with paste handling.
- A numeric field that is not a code, like a quantity; use `input type="number"`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input-otp
```

The component wraps [`input-otp`](https://github.com/guilhermerodz/input-otp),
which owns the single hidden input, paste handling, and the caret position.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  InputOTP,
  InputOTPGroup,
  InputOTPSeparator,
  InputOTPSlot,
} from "@/components/cadence/input-otp/input-otp";

export function Code() {
  return (
    <InputOTP maxLength={6} aria-label="Verification code">
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
      <InputOTPSeparator />
      <InputOTPGroup>
        <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={4} />
        <InputOTPSlot index={5} />
      </InputOTPGroup>
    </InputOTP>
  );
}
```

`maxLength` must equal the number of slots. Each `InputOTPSlot` needs its `index`.

## Examples

### Controlled, with completion

```tsx
const [code, setCode] = useState("");

<InputOTP maxLength={6} value={code} onChange={setCode} onComplete={verify}>
  …
</InputOTP>;
```

`onComplete` fires once the last slot is filled. It is the right place to submit
the code, not an effect that watches `code.length`.

### Invalid

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={4} aria-label="Code" aria-invalid>
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} aria-invalid />
    …
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>
```

`aria-invalid` on a slot styles its border; the text beside the field carries the
message.

### Disabled

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={6} disabled aria-label="Code">
  …
</InputOTP>
```

### Without a separator

```tsx
<InputOTP maxLength={4} aria-label="PIN" containerClassName="justify-center">
  <InputOTPGroup>
    <InputOTPSlot index={0} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={1} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={2} />
    <InputOTPSlot index={3} />
  </InputOTPGroup>
</InputOTP>
```

## API

### `InputOTP`

| Prop               | Type                        | Default | Description                                    |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `maxLength`        | `number`                    | –       | Required. Number of characters.                |
| `value`            | `string`                    | –       | Controlled value.                              |
| `defaultValue`     | `string`                    | –       | Uncontrolled initial value.                    |
| `onChange`         | `(value: string) => void`   | –       | Fired on every change, including paste.        |
| `onComplete`       | `(value: string) => void`   | –       | Fired when the code is full.                   |
| `disabled`         | `boolean`                   | `false` | Ignores input.                                 |
| `containerClassName` | `string`                  | –       | Classes for the wrapper that positions the slots. |
| `className`        | `string`                    | –       | Classes for the input itself.                  |

### `InputOTPSlot`

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                          |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `index`     | `number` | –       | Required. Which character it shows.  |
| `className` | `string` | –       | Merged last.                         |

`InputOTPGroup` and `InputOTPSeparator` are plain wrappers with `data-slot` values
`input-otp-group` and `input-otp-separator`.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `state.morph`. A character lands in its slot with a short fade and settles
from 0.96 to full size. Deleting a character is instant — an exit animation would
leave a ghost in a field the user is racing against.

| Phase   | Properties                        | Token         | Interruptible |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| type    | `opacity 0 → 1`, `scale 0.96 → 1` | `state.morph` | yes           |
| delete  | none (instant)                    | –             | –             |
| reduced | `opacity` only                    | `state.morph` | yes           |
| none    | no transition                     | –             | –             |

The caret is drawn but does not blink. A blink is a continuous loop that would
have to be declared as `data.transition`; the active slot's ring already shows
where the next character goes, so the loop buys nothing.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys              | Action                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any character     | Fills the active slot and advances.                       |
| `Backspace`       | Clears the current slot, then moves back.                 |
| `Arrow Left/Right`| Moves the active slot without changing the value.         |
| `Cmd/Ctrl + V`    | Pastes the whole code, filling every slot from the start. |

## Accessibility

- `input-otp` renders a single real input with `aria-label` and
  `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so assistive technology sees one field, not six.
- The slots are visual mirrors; they are not focusable and carry no role.
- `onComplete` is where the code is judged. The component never decides that a
  code is wrong.
- Keep the field visible while verifying and announce the result next to it, not
  through the slots' animation.

## Validation and data ownership

| The component does                                  | You do                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Styles `aria-invalid` on the slots                  | Deciding that the code is wrong or expired        |
| Reports every change and the completed value        | Verifying the code and mapping the server error   |
| Keeps the paste path working                        | Re-sending a code, throttling attempts            |

There is no `validate`, `schema`, or `rules` prop. See [validation](/docs/validation).

## Responsive behavior

Slots are 36px squares; six of them plus a separator fit a 320px viewport. For
longer codes, drop the separator group or reduce the gap in `containerClassName`
before shrinking the slots below 32px.

## Performance

One Motion element per slot, animating `opacity` and `transform` only when a
character changes. No per-keystroke layout read: the caret position comes from the
input, not from measurement.

## Notes for AI

- `maxLength` and the slot count must agree; a mismatch silently drops characters.
- Use `onComplete` to submit, not an effect that watches `value.length`.
- The caret does not blink on purpose. Do not re-add a `animate-caret-blink`
  loop without declaring the recipe.

# Progress

Displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task.

## When to use

- Work with a measurable end: an upload, an import, a multi-step build.
- Work long enough that the user would otherwise wonder whether anything is
  happening, and short enough that they will watch the bar.
- A determinate value next to other numbers, where the bar is a second reading of
  the same fact.

## When not to use

- Work of unknown duration. Pass `value={null}` for an indeterminate bar, or use
  `spinner` when there is no bar to fill.
- A page that is simply loading its own content; use `skeleton`.
- A value that is not progressing toward an end, like a score. Render the number.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/progress
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { Progress } from "@/components/cadence/progress/progress";

export function Upload() {
  return <Progress value={40} aria-label="Uploading assets" />;
}
```

`value` is required and may be `null` for indeterminate work. `Progress` renders
its own track and indicator; `ProgressLabel` and `ProgressValue` go inside it as
children.

## Examples

### Labelled, with the number

```tsx
<Progress value={uploaded} aria-label="Uploading assets">
  <div className="flex w-full items-center justify-between">
    <ProgressLabel>Uploading assets</ProgressLabel>
    <ProgressValue />
  </div>
</Progress>
```

`ProgressValue` formats the value with `Intl.NumberFormat`; pass `format` or
`locale` to the root to change it.

### Indeterminate

```tsx
<Progress value={null} aria-label="Preparing preview" />
```

The fill fills the track and pulses. There is no sweep: a moving gradient says
"indeterminate" with motion alone, which is exactly the anti-pattern in the motion
system.

### Custom range

```tsx
<Progress value={3} min={0} max={5} aria-label="Step 3 of 5">
  <ProgressValue />
</Progress>
```

`ProgressValue` renders `60%` for `3/5`; use `getAriaValueText` if you want "step 3
of 5" announced instead.

### Composed track

```tsx
<Progress value={72} aria-label="Storage">
  <ProgressTrack className="h-1.5 bg-muted">
    <ProgressIndicator className="bg-emerald-500" />
  </ProgressTrack>
</Progress>
```

Composing the track yourself replaces the default one. The indicator still reads
the value from the root, so it keeps animating.

## API

### `Progress`

| Prop              | Type                                  | Default | Description                                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `value`           | `number \| null`                      | –       | Required. `null` means indeterminate.        |
| `min`, `max`      | `number`                              | `0`, `100` | Range.                                    |
| `format`          | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`            | –       | How `ProgressValue` formats the number.      |
| `getAriaValueText`| `(value, raw) => string`              | –       | Human-readable value for assistive tech.     |
| `className`       | `string`                              | –       | Merged last; the default is a wrap layout.   |

### `ProgressTrack`, `ProgressIndicator`, `ProgressLabel`, `ProgressValue`

Plain wrappers over Base UI's parts; each forwards `className` and native props.
`ProgressIndicator` carries the motion.

## Motion contract

Recipe: `data.transition`, in both of its documented forms.

| Phase         | Properties                     | Token            | Interruptible |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------- | ------------- |
| value change  | `scaleX old → new` (one-shot)  | `data.transition`| yes           |
| indeterminate | `opacity` pulse (continuous)   | `data.transition`| yes           |
| reduced       | value jumps; pulse kept, opacity only | `data.transition` | yes     |
| none          | no transition, `animate-none`  | –                | –             |

The fill is a `scaleX` transform on an element that keeps the full track width, so
a value change never triggers layout. Under `reduced` the fill jumps to the new
value — position is information, the animation is not — while the indeterminate
pulse survives, because opacity-only loading feedback is what M5 keeps.

## Keyboard interactions

No keyboard interaction: the progress bar is not focusable. If the user can cancel
the work, put a `button` next to it.

## Accessibility

- Base UI puts `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, and
  `aria-valuenow` on the root; `value={null}` omits `aria-valuenow`.
- Give it a name with `aria-label`, or render `ProgressLabel` inside the root and
  let Base UI wire it.
- Announce completion outside the bar (text or `toast`); a full bar is not
  announced by a screen reader on its own.
- Never hide the percentage behind the animation: `ProgressValue` is the readable
  copy of the same fact.

## Responsive behavior

The bar fills its container and stays 8px tall at every breakpoint. When it sits in
a card header, keep the label and value on one line and let the bar take the next
line — the default `flex-wrap` layout does this without extra classes.

## Performance

One Motion element. A determinate update animates a transform; an indeterminate bar
runs a CSS opacity loop that the compositor owns, so a page with several bars does
not schedule main-thread frames. Avoid driving `value` from `requestAnimationFrame`
yourself; pass the real value and let the transition smooth it.

## Notes for AI

- `value` is required; pass `null` for indeterminate, never `undefined`.
- Use `scaleX`, not width. A width transition relayouts the track every frame.
- For work with no measurable end and no bar, use `spinner`, not a fake percentage.

# Alert Dialog

A modal confirmation that interrupts the flow and needs an explicit choice before anything happens.

## When to use

- A destructive or irreversible action — deleting a project, revoking a key, overwriting a draft — that the
  user must confirm on purpose.
- A decision the page cannot make for the user: move the workspace, leave without saving, end the session.
- A step that must be acknowledged before anything else continues, where an accidental dismissal would be
  the bug.

## When not to use

- A task with more than one decision or a form to fill in. Use `dialog`: it can be dismissed, and it should be.
- A message that does not block anything. Use `alert` where it belongs on the page, or `toast` for a moment.
- A hint attached to a control. Use `tooltip`.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/alert-dialog
```

This also installs `button`, which the two actions render through.

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/alert-dialog/alert-dialog";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function DeleteProject() {
  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Delete project</AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            Every deployment and its logs go with it. This cannot be undone.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel>Keep project</AlertDialogCancel>
          <AlertDialogAction variant="destructive">Delete project</AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### A compact confirmation

`size="sm"` caps the panel at `max-w-xs` and turns the footer into a two-column grid, which is what a
yes/no question looks like. The dialog is centred and its header is centred with it.

```tsx
<AlertDialogContent size="sm">
  <AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogTitle>Archive this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
    <AlertDialogDescription>It stops deploying. You can unarchive it later.</AlertDialogDescription>
  </AlertDialogHeader>
  <AlertDialogFooter>
    <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
    <AlertDialogAction>Archive</AlertDialogAction>
  </AlertDialogFooter>
</AlertDialogContent>
```

### With an icon

`AlertDialogMedia` is a slot, not a decoration: put an icon in it and the header switches to the
left-aligned, icon-first layout on `size="default"`.

```tsx
<AlertDialogHeader>
  <AlertDialogMedia>
    <Trash2 aria-hidden="true" />
  </AlertDialogMedia>
  <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
  <AlertDialogDescription>Every deployment goes with it.</AlertDialogDescription>
</AlertDialogHeader>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertDialogContent>…</AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;
```

### A confirmation that is still working

The component never owns a request. The caller passes the in-flight state, and the library keeps the
button a button:

```tsx
<AlertDialogAction disabled={isDeleting} onClick={() => mutate()}>
  {isDeleting ? "Deleting…" : "Delete project"}
</AlertDialogAction>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `onOpenChangeComplete` | Base UI root. Always modal; pointer dismissal is fixed off. |
| `AlertDialogTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Opens the dialog. |
| `AlertDialogContent` | `size` (`"default" \| "sm"`), `render`, `className` | Renders portal, overlay, and popup. |
| `AlertDialogOverlay` | `className` | Only needed when replacing `AlertDialogContent`. |
| `AlertDialogHeader` / `AlertDialogFooter` | `className` | Layout only. |
| `AlertDialogMedia` | `className` | Icon slot; changes the header layout. |
| `AlertDialogTitle` | `className` | Required accessible name. |
| `AlertDialogDescription` | `className` | Supporting text; wire it to the decision, not the product. |
