| `AlertDialogAction` | `variant`, `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Confirming button. Closes the dialog after `onClick` runs. |
| `AlertDialogCancel` | `variant` (`outline`), `size`, `onClick`, `render` | Dismissing button. Also closes the dialog. |

Both buttons render Base UI's `Close`, so a confirmation ends the dialog instead of leaving it open —
upstream's Base UI port binds neither button, which would make the default usage a no-op.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | overlay `opacity 0 → 1`; panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` / `duration.base` | yes |
| exit | overlay `opacity → 0`; panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so no transition runs | – | – |

The entrance is the dialog's, because this is the same popup: a fade under a 0.96-scale settle. The
motion is CSS-only — Base UI toggles `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` and the class list
reads the duration tokens — so there is no JavaScript animation loop and nothing to interrupt by hand.
Reopening during the exit reverses the fade rather than restarting it.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Cycles focus inside the dialog. Focus never reaches the page behind it. |
| Escape | Cancels: the dialog closes and focus returns to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the focused button — confirm or cancel, whichever has focus. |

The outside press is the one path that is deliberately missing: clicking the overlay does nothing,
which is the difference between this component and `dialog`.

## Accessibility

- Base UI provides `role="alertdialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, focus
  trapping, focus return, scroll lock, and the Escape path.
- `AlertDialogTitle` is required: an alert dialog without an accessible name is invalid, and it is
  announced as the first thing inside the popup. `AlertDialogDescription` becomes the description, so
  put the consequence there, not in a second paragraph.
- Focus lands on the cancel control, the first tabbable element inside the popup, not on the destructive
  action — so a stray Enter cancels rather than confirms. Put `AlertDialogCancel` first in the footer for
  that reason; the footer's column-reverse layout still shows the confirming action on top.
- Destructive styling is colour plus a specific verb ("Delete project", not "OK"). Never rely on the
  red alone; the label has to carry the meaning in greyscale and in a screen reader.
- `AlertDialogMedia` is decorative when the title already says what happened. Mark the icon
  `aria-hidden="true"` unless it is the only signal.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is centred with a 1rem gutter on narrow viewports: `max-w-lg` for the default size and
`max-w-xs` for `size="sm"`. The footer stacks its buttons in reverse DOM order (the confirming action
on top) below `sm`, and becomes a row that ends on the right above it. With `size="sm"` the two
buttons split the width instead of stacking, so the two answers stay side by side at every size.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the overlay and panel unmount after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `width`/`height` transition, and no
  JavaScript animation running while the dialog sits open.
- `AlertDialogAction` and `AlertDialogCancel` are ordinary `Button`s, so the press feedback is the
  button's (a 0.97 scale that the same motion mode can drop).

## Notes for AI

- Reach for `alert-dialog` only when the answer must be deliberate. A form, a longer task, or anything
  the user may want to dismiss belongs in `dialog`.
- Always render `AlertDialogTitle`; it is the accessible name. Use `AlertDialogDescription` for the
  consequence of the action, in one sentence.
- Name the confirming button after its effect ("Delete project", "Leave without saving"), never "OK".
- Both buttons close the dialog, so never hide the dialog manually in `onClick`; pass the work to the
  caller instead.
- Use `AlertDialogMedia` for an icon, not for an illustration: the slot is a 4rem square that changes
  the header layout.

# Popover

An anchored panel that opens next to its trigger and returns focus to it when it closes.

## When to use

- A small set of controls that belongs to the thing it is attached to: column visibility, a filter, a
  share link, a colour picker.
- Context that would crowd the page if it were always visible, but that the user opens on demand.
- An edit that is scoped to one trigger and can be dismissed without losing the page.

## When not to use

- A confirmation that must be answered. Use `alert-dialog`: a popover can be dismissed by clicking away.
- A task that needs the whole screen or a focus trap. Use `dialog` or `sheet`.
- A one- or two-word hint on a control. Use `tooltip`, which cannot hold interactive content.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/popover
```

## Usage

```tsx
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverHeader,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from "@/components/cadence/popover/popover";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function SharePopover() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Share</PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent>
        <PopoverHeader>
          <PopoverTitle>Share this project</PopoverTitle>
          <PopoverDescription>Anyone with the link can read it, nobody can edit it.</PopoverDescription>
        </PopoverHeader>
        <p className="text-sm">cadence.dev/p/cadence-ui</p>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Positioned by side

`side` and `align` choose the placement, and the panel flips when there is no room. The motion follows
the anchor, not the side: the panel grows from `--transform-origin`, which Base UI points at the
trigger.

```tsx
<PopoverContent side="top" align="start" sideOffset={8}>
  …
</PopoverContent>
```

### With a form

The panel is a normal container, so `Field` and `Input` work inside it. Nothing traps focus: a popover
is non-modal by default.

```tsx
<PopoverContent>
  <PopoverHeader>
    <PopoverTitle>Rename this view</PopoverTitle>
  </PopoverHeader>
  <Field>
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="view-name">Name</FieldLabel>
    <Input id="view-name" defaultValue="Open PRs" />
  </Field>
</PopoverContent>
```

### Controlled

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Popover open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <PopoverContent>…</PopoverContent>
</Popover>;
```

### Modal when it has to be

A popover that holds a destructive control can trap focus and block the page behind it without becoming
a dialog:

```tsx
<Popover modal>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Danger zone</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>…</PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Popover` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` | Base UI root. Non-modal by default. |
| `PopoverTrigger` | native button props, `render` | The anchor and the toggle. |
| `PopoverContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal and positioner; `sideOffset` defaults to `4`. |
| `PopoverHeader` | `className` | Stacked title and description. |
| `PopoverTitle` | `className` | Base UI heading; the panel's accessible name. |
| `PopoverDescription` | `className` | Muted supporting text; becomes `aria-describedby`. |

`PopoverContent` positions itself; there is no `PopoverAnchor` export, because Base UI anchors to the
trigger and upstream's Base UI surface has no anchor part.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes (reopen mid-exit) |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – |

The panel grows out of its anchor rather than sliding towards it. A slide would need a distance token
and four per-side classes, and it moves the edge the positioner just lined up away from the trigger;
`--transform-origin` says the same thing with one transform. The scale reads `--motion-scale-in`, so
the class list carries a token and not a number.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Opens the popover from its trigger. |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Moves through the panel's controls and then out of it; focus is not trapped unless `modal`. |
| Escape | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. |

Pressing outside closes it, which is the difference between a popover and an alert dialog.

## Accessibility

- Base UI gives the popup `role="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` on the trigger, `aria-controls`, and focus
  return on close. The panel is labelled by `PopoverTitle` and described by `PopoverDescription` when
  both are rendered.
- The trigger keeps `aria-expanded` in step, so assistive technology announces "collapsed" / "expanded"
  rather than a dialog appearing out of nowhere.
- `PopoverTitle` is optional for an interactive panel, but any popover that opens a region of controls
  should have one: an unnamed dialog is announced as just "dialog".
- Interactive controls inside the panel are reachable: the popover is non-modal, so Tab leaves it and
  the trigger's focus ring stays where the user left it.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is `w-72` wide and flips sides when the trigger has no room above or below; Base UI also
shifts it along the cross axis to stay inside the viewport. On a narrow screen it can fill most of the
width — pass `className="w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]"` or a max width when the content is wider than the
default.

## Performance

- One popup tree is mounted only while open; the portal unmounts after the exit transition.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript
  animation loop. Reopening during the exit reverses the fade.

## Notes for AI

- Use `popover` for anchored, dismissible content; use `alert-dialog` when the answer must be explicit.
- Pass the trigger through `render`, not a wrapper: the trigger is what the positioner anchors to and
  what gets `aria-expanded`.
- Do not simulate a modal confirmation with `modal`; it blocks outside interaction but still closes on
  Escape, which is not what a confirmation promises.

# Tooltip

A short label that names a control on hover or focus, and disappears when the pointer leaves.

## When to use

- An icon-only control whose meaning is not obvious from the icon alone.
- The full value behind a truncated label, or a keyboard shortcut next to an action.
- A hint that helps the first use of a dense control and is useless once learned.

## When not to use

- Anything the user must read to act: a tooltip disappears on scroll, touch, and Escape. If the content
  matters, put it on the page or in a `popover`.
- Interactive content. A tooltip cannot hold a button or a link; use `popover`.
- The accessible name of a button that already has text. Two labels that disagree is worse than one.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/tooltip
```

Optionally wrap the app in `TooltipProvider` once to set one delay for every tooltip; Base UI does not
require it.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip/tooltip";
import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button/button";

export function BoldTooltip() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider delay={200}>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon-sm" />} aria-label="Bold">
          <Bold />
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>Bold (⌘B)</TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Side and alignment

`side` defaults to `top` and the label flips when there is no room. The arrow moves with it; the panel
grows out of `--transform-origin`, so the scale starts where the trigger meets the label.

```tsx
<TooltipContent side="right" align="start">
  Right, aligned to the start
</TooltipContent>
```

### A delay for the whole app

`TooltipProvider` sets the delay once. Without it, Base UI's own default applies.

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delay={300}>
  <App />
</TooltipProvider>
```

### Disabled controls

A disabled button does not emit pointer events, so wrap it and put the hint on the wrapper:

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<span className="inline-flex" />}>
    <Button disabled>Deploy</Button>
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Finish the required fields first</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TooltipProvider` | `delay` | Optional. One delay for every tooltip inside. |
| `Tooltip` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange` | Base UI root. |
| `TooltipTrigger` | native button props, `render` | Hover or focus target; carries `aria-describedby`. |
| `TooltipContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, popup, and arrow. `side` defaults to `top`, `sideOffset` to `4`. |

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | label `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | label `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the label appears on the first frame | – | – |

A tooltip is small enough that `duration.fast` is already at the edge of readable: nothing here waits
for an exit to finish. The arrow is part of the popup and moves with it, so it is never animated
separately.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focus shows the label; leaving hides it. |
| Escape | Hides the label and leaves focus on the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Activates the trigger. The tooltip does not swallow the press. |

Hover alone is never the only path: the tooltip opens on keyboard focus too, which is what makes it
usable on touch and from a screen reader.

## Accessibility

- Base UI's own tooltip adds neither `role="tooltip"` nor `aria-describedby`; Cadence wires both. The
  trigger points at the popup only while it is open — a closed popup would otherwise leave a dangling
  id, which axe reports — and the popup is `role="tooltip"`.
- The tooltip must not be the only name of a control. Give an icon button a real `aria-label`; the
  tooltip is the extra sentence, not the name.
- Text stays readable in both themes: `bg-foreground` / `text-background` invert, so the label keeps
  contrast against whatever surface it floats over.
- Escape dismisses it without moving focus, so a tooltip never traps a keyboard user.

## Responsive behavior

The label is `w-fit` with a `max-w-xs` cap and wraps at word boundaries (`text-balance`) instead of
running off screen. Base UI flips the side and shifts the alignment when the viewport cannot fit it.

## Performance

- The popup tree is mounted only while the label is open; a page can carry dozens of tooltips without
  paying for them all.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only — no layout read, no measuring loop, no JavaScript animation.
  Hover is not a state the component polls.

## Notes for AI

- Use a tooltip to name or explain a control, never to deliver information the user needs to proceed.
- Do not put a link, button, or form inside it; use `popover`.
- Give every icon-only trigger an `aria-label`: the tooltip complements the name, it does not replace it.

# Hover Card

A preview panel that opens from a link on hover or focus and disappears when the pointer leaves.

## When to use

- A preview of what a link leads to: a profile, a repository, a document — enough to decide whether to
  click.
- Context that helps a name make sense — the person behind an `@handle`, the project behind a package.
- A short panel with one or two actions that should not interrupt the page.

## When not to use

- A label for an icon. Use `tooltip`: it is smaller, quicker, and announced as a description.
- Content the user opened on purpose. Use `popover`: hover cards close when the pointer moves on, and
  anything with a task in it deserves a deliberate open.
- Information the user needs to answer a question. Nothing that appears and disappears on hover can be
  the only place it lives.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/hover-card
```

## Usage

```tsx
import { HoverCard, HoverCardContent, HoverCardTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/hover-card/hover-card";

export function ReviewerCard() {
  return (
    <p>
      Reviewed by{" "}
      <HoverCard>
        <HoverCardTrigger render={<a href="/u/linruoxin" />}>@linruoxin</HoverCardTrigger>
        <HoverCardContent>
          <p className="text-sm font-medium">Lin Ruoxin</p>
          <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Maintains the motion layer and the registry.</p>
        </HoverCardContent>
      </HoverCard>
    </p>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### With an action inside

The card is not modal and does not trap focus, so a link or a button inside it works normally. Base UI
keeps the card open while the pointer or focus is inside it, which is what makes the action reachable.

```tsx
<HoverCardContent>
  <p className="text-sm font-medium">Lin Ruoxin</p>
  <Button size="xs" variant="secondary">
    Follow
  </Button>
</HoverCardContent>
```

### Placement

`side` defaults to `bottom` — unlike a tooltip, which defaults to `top` — because the card is larger and
reads better below the link. `alignOffset` defaults to `4` for the same reason.

```tsx
<HoverCardContent side="right" align="start">
  …
</HoverCardContent>
```

### A delay for the whole app

`HoverCard` takes the same delay props as the Base UI root. A longer `delay` keeps a page of links from
flashing cards at every pointer movement.

```tsx
<HoverCard delay={400}>…</HoverCard>
```

## API

| Part | Props | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HoverCard` | `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `delay`, `closeDelay` | Base UI root; `delay` is per card. |
| `HoverCardTrigger` | native props, `render` | The link or button the card describes. |
| `HoverCardContent` | `side`, `align`, `sideOffset`, `alignOffset`, `render`, `className` | Renders portal, positioner, and popup. `side` defaults to `bottom`, `sideOffset` to `4`, `alignOffset` to `4`. |

The portal renders `data-slot="hover-card-portal"`; the popup is `data-slot="hover-card-content"`. There
is no `HoverCardArrow`: upstream's Base UI surface has none, and the card is a surface rather than a
pointer.

## Motion contract

| Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | panel `opacity 0 → 1` + `scale 0.96 → 1` from the anchor origin | `popup.anchored` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| exit | panel `opacity → 0` + `scale → 0.96` | `exit.fade` · `duration.fast` | yes |
| reduced | opacity only, no scale; the duration tokens run at 0.6× (96ms) | `exit.fade` | yes |
| none | every `--motion-duration-*` resolves to `0ms`, so the panel appears on the first frame | – | – |

Same anchored motion as `popover` and `tooltip`: the scale starts at `--transform-origin`, which Base UI
points at the trigger. Hover cards close when the pointer leaves, so the exit has to be short; `fast` is
the anchored-surface duration the three share.

## Keyboard interactions

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Focusing the trigger opens the card; moving focus into it keeps it open. |
| Escape | Closes the card and returns focus to the trigger. |
| Enter / Space | Follows the trigger link, or activates a control inside the card. |

Keyboard focus opens the card for the same reason it does in a tooltip: without it, the content would
exist only for pointer users.

## Accessibility

- The trigger carries the accessible name; the card is supplementary. That is why Cadence does not give
  the popup `role="dialog"` or wire it as the trigger's description: a panel that may hold several
  paragraphs and a button is neither a name nor a description, and a screen reader reading it on every
  focus would be noise.
- Interactive content inside the card is reachable in order: Tab moves from the trigger into the card's
  links and buttons, and the card stays open while focus is inside it.
- Hover is never the only path: focus opens it too, and Escape closes it, so the card never traps a
  keyboard user.
- If the card is the only place a piece of information exists, it is in the wrong component — move it
  into the page or into a `popover`.

## Responsive behavior

The panel is `w-64` with `p-4`; Base UI flips it to another side and shifts the alignment when the
viewport cannot fit it. On touch devices there is no hover: the trigger still opens the card on focus or
tap, and the content must not assume a pointer is nearby.

## Performance

- Mounted only while open, so a page of links carries no extra popup trees.
- Animates `opacity` and `scale` only: no layout reads, no `top`/`left` transition, no JavaScript
  animation loop. The card follows the anchor through the positioner, not through React state.

## Notes for AI

- Use `hover-card` only for a preview of the linked thing; use `popover` for anything the user opens to
  act, and `tooltip` for a label.
- The trigger must have its own text or `aria-label`; the card is not its name.
- Keep the card small: a person, a repository, a document summary, one action. If it needs scrolling, it
  wants to be a `popover` or a page.
